title: Tensor lookup in tiles
author: vermorel
body: The Facebook Tensor Comprehensions allows the implementation of  Lookup Table Embeddings  (see page 20 of the paper), to allow, for example: def 2LUT(float(E1,D) LUT1, int(B,L1) I1,   float(E2,D) LUT2, int(B,L2) I2) → (O1, O2) {     O1(i,j) +=! LUT1(I1(i,k),j)     O2(i,j) +=! LUT2(I2(i,k),j) }  Those tensor lookups are of primary importance in order to remove the need for sparse linear algebra. I would be very nice if the tile language was supporting those look-ups.

title: Support efficient concatenates in Stripe: Efficient Densenet Support
author: kazimuth
body: DenseNets are typically implemented with long strings of concatenations, which require O(n^2) time for O(n) convolutions just for memory copies. If the memory can be pre-allocated and then sliced, the operation will be significantly faster. See, e.g. this paper. I'm curious if PlaidML could support this mode of operation.

title: Sign function in the plaidml backend.py
author: skchao74
body: Hi, I tried to use the sign function defined in the backend.py  https://github.com/plaidml/plaidml/blob/master/plaidml/keras/backend.py. It took me a while to notice that the definition of the sign function in that file is different from what people usually expect. The sign function here is a clip function that takes the numbers outside [-1,1] interval to either -1 and 1, depending on their sign, but leaves everything inside (-1,1) as is. For example, inputting -0.5 outputs -0.5 rather than -1, and inputting 0.3 outputs 0.3 rather than 1, etc. Maybe there are some deeper reasons for it or based on some conventions, but I only feel this may be a little confusing. Thank you.

title: Solved: plaidml-setup throws SyntaxError: invalid syntax on line 1320 or 1332 (MacOS)
author: jongwooc
body: #321 change in plaidML/__init__py line 1320 or 1332(on my version of PlaidML) class Shape(_Shape): def __init__(self, ctx, dtype, *args, layout=None):  into this class Shape(_Shape): def __init__(self, ctx, dtype, layout=None, *args):  it's just simple python2 syntax problem that all the arguments should be located before  "*args". (not sure about python3)  This will raise 'int' object has no attribute 'encode' error on actual python2 plaidML including plaidbench.  The second error is caused by changing the position of class Shape(_Shape): def init(self, ctx, dtype, *args, layout=None): so change plaidML/keras/backend.py line 1734 tensor = plaidml.Tensor(_device(), plaidml.Shape(_ctx, ptile.convert_np_dtype_to_pml(dtype), *value.shape))  into tensor = plaidml.Tensor(_device(), plaidml.Shape(_ctx, ptile.convert_np_dtype_to_pml(dtype), None, *value.shape))  Which is just adding None for the changed position. As the location of layout=None has been changed, *value.shape right after ptile.convert_np_dtype_to_pml(dtype) will pass it's [0] value to the layout, and adding None value for the new layout location will solve the problem for now. Hope Plaid team eventually fix this bug and make Plaid better compatible with Python2.(Although it will be depreciated soon.)

title: Keras 2.3.0 last release to support multi-backend Keras
author: cfox570
body: From KERAS.IO DOES THIS PREVENT PLAIDML FROM SUPPORTING KERAS IN THE FUTURE? Multi-backend Keras and tf.keras: At this time, we recommend that Keras users who use multi-backend Keras with the TensorFlow backend switch to tf.keras in TensorFlow 2.0. tf.keras is better maintained and has better integration with TensorFlow features (eager execution, distribution support and other). Keras 2.2.5 was the last release of Keras implementing the 2.2.* API. It was the last release to only support TensorFlow 1 (as well as Theano and CNTK). The current release is Keras 2.3.0, which makes significant API changes and add support for TensorFlow 2.0. The 2.3.0 release will be the last major release of multi-backend Keras. Multi-backend Keras is superseded by tf.keras. Bugs present in multi-backend Keras will only be fixed until April 2020 (as part of minor releases). For more information about the future of Keras, see the Keras meeting notes.

title: Trying to understand the role of executable.{cc,h}, program.{cc,h}, registry.{cc,h}
author: harsh-nod
body: I'm taking a look at the code in branch plaidml-v1 to better understand how the code is being migrated to MLIR. In pmlc/tools/pmlc-jit there exists pmlc-jit.cc which seems similar to mlir_cpu_runner (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/master/mlir/tools/mlir-cpu-runner/mlir-cpu-runner.cpp). However, rather than just use mlir::JitRunnerMain, the code here creates instances of type Executable and Program instead. Looking at the code for Executable, it seems that each LLVM function is being replaced with an interface function for a unified invocation interface. Why is this required (since mlir_cpu_runner doesn't do this)? Also, there is a struct MemRefDescriptor that the function arguments are cast into. Since all the examples are lowered to the llvm Dialect before being JIT-ed why do we need this? (since there is no concept of memref in the llvm Dialect?) Thanks!

title: MultiGPU support
author: gajdosech2
body: Hello, first off, I really like this project, thanks a lot for your development time! The fact I can train networks with Keras using basically any underlying GPU is wonderful. I have tested this on Windows 10 using RTX 2060, GTX 1060 and RX 470. Works flawlessly on all of them. However, I am tinkering around with a 3 x RX 470 PC and would really like to utilize all the GPUs, not just the one. From what I understand (and from reading other issues) I understand that multi-gpu support (something like tensorflow's mirrored strategy) is not yet implemented. Therefore I would like to ask - is there any road map for this feature? Is it possible that support for multi-GPU AMD systems will be added anytime soon? Thanks for answer!

title: ArgMax giving incorrect results for indices greater than 255
author: sanketdiwale
body: I found that the ArgMax op is giving incorrect results whenever the index result for argmax is greater than 255. I saw this incorrect behavior while using plaidml (version 0.6.4 and version 0.7.0) as a backend to keras from python with device : "opencl_nvidia_geforce_gt_650m.0" on MacBook Pro. (Haven't tested this in other environments). Below is an example code to reproduce the error import os os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "plaidml.keras.backend" import keras from keras import backend as K  # works fine for indices less than 255 r1 = K.arange(start=0,stop=20,dtype=K.floatx())  print(K.eval(K.argmax(r1)))  # outputs '19' correctly  r2 = K.arange(start=0,stop=300,dtype=K.floatx())    print(K.eval(K.argmax(r2)))  # outputs '43' instead of the expected result '299'  r2 = K.arange(start=0,stop=257,dtype=K.floatx())  print(K.eval(K.argmax(r2)))  # outputs '0' instead of the expected result '256'  r2 = K.arange(start=0,stop=259,dtype=K.floatx()) print(K.eval(K.argmax(r2)))  # outputs '2' instead of the expected result '258'  r2 = K.arange(start=0,stop=255,dtype=K.floatx())      print(K.eval(K.argmax(r2)))  # outputs '254' correctly It seems there might be some type of overflow errors or type cast errors somewhere in the ArgMax implementation.

body: I am using plaidml as a backend to keras in python 3.6. I tested this bug with plaidml versions 0.6.4 and 0.7.0 installed from the pip repository. Code to reproduce error: import os os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "plaidml.keras.backend" import keras from keras import backend as K import numpy as np  # generate a random numpy vector x = np.random.rand(10,19)  # convert the numpy vector to a tensor as used by the plaidml backend  x = K.constant(x)  # slice the vector to get the first element of x  y = x[0,0]  print(K.eval(y)) print(y.shape) This gives out the wrong value for 'y'. It always returns the value to be 0. irrespective of the actual value of the element x[0,0]. This error is observed whenever trying to get a single scalar element from the vector using a slice. When trying to retrieve non-scalar results, the slicing seems to work fine. This seems to be affecting results when trying to implement custom functions using the plaidml backend. Would be great if someone from the developer team could look into this and point us to the appropriate fix for the issue. Best regards.

title: Upsample2D does not work consistenly between Tensorflow 2.2.0 and PlaidML
author: mostergaardd
body: I've noticed that upsampling with bilinear interpolation does not behave consistently between Tensorflow and PlaidML. Generally, when upsampling a simple square shape, PlaidML produces a square that is translated up and left compared to Tensorflow. This is a serious issue for us, since we are using PlaidML to deploy models trained in Tensorflow. We expect to have the exact same behavour in development and deployment for our models. Libraries: numpy == 1.19.0 keras == 2.2.4 plaidml-keras == 0.7.0 tensorflow == 2.2.0  Code to reproduce: import os  import numpy as np   os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "plaidml.keras.backend" import keras from keras import backend as K import tensorflow as tf  print(tf.__version__)  # 2.2.0 print(keras.__version__) # 2.2.4  # the operations tensorflow_upsample_nearest = tf.keras.layers.UpSampling2D(size=(2, 2), interpolation='nearest') plaidml_upsample_nearest = keras.layers.UpSampling2D(size=(2, 2), interpolation='nearest')  tensorflow_upsample_bil = tf.keras.layers.UpSampling2D(size=(2, 2), interpolation='bilinear') plaidml_upsample_bil = keras.layers.UpSampling2D(size=(2, 2), interpolation='bilinear')  # initialize a sample image hw = 16 sq_0 = hw//3 sq_1 = 2 * hw//3  x = np.zeros((1,hw,hw,1))  x[:,sq_0:sq_1, sq_0:sq_1, :] = 1 x_tensor = K.variable(value=x)  # run the operations y_tf_nearest = tensorflow_upsample_nearest(x).numpy()[0,:,:,0] y_tf_bil = tensorflow_upsample_bil(x).numpy()[0,:,:,0]  y_pl_nearest = plaidml_upsample_nearest(x_tensor).eval()[0,:,:,0] y_pl_bil = plaidml_upsample_bil(x_tensor).eval()[0,:,:,0]  # get the difference diff_nearest = (y_tf_nearest - y_pl_nearest) diff_bilinear = (y_tf_bil - y_pl_bil)  # assert that the diff is all zeros assert np.all(diff_nearest == 0), "Nearest interpolation is not equal" assert np.all(diff_bilinear == 0), "Bilinear interpolation is not equal"

title: [comp] Add allocated memory reuse
author: kdobros
body: Add optimization that removes comp.alloc where previously allocated and deallocated memory can be used. Input: %mem = comp.alloc %env %host // (1) operations on %mem %ev1 = comp.schedule_read %host from %mem on %env comp.wait %ev comp.dealloc %env %mem %new_mem = comp.alloc %env %host // (2) operations on %new_mem %ev2 = comp.schedule_read %host from %new_mem on %env Possible output: %mem = comp.alloc %env %host // (1) operations on %mem %ev1 = comp.schedule_read %host from %mem on %env comp.wait %ev %ev2 = comp.schedule_write %host to %mem on %env // (2) operations on %mem %ev3 = comp.schedule_read %host from %mem on %env Please not that redundant read -> write and wait should be handled by separate pass.

title: [comp] Add pass to remove redundant memory transfers
author: kdobros
body: Add pass that removes patterns of schedule_read and schedule_write operations that don't have any visible effects. Example input: %ev = comp.schedule_read %host from %mem on %env // Operations not modifying %host or %mem comp.schedule_write %host to %mem on %env wait for %ev Possible output: %ev = comp.schedule_read %host from %mem on %env // Operations not modifying %host or %mem ^ Write can be removed as %host and %mem are already in sync because of schedule_read.

title: [comp] Add pass to recalculate event dependencies
author: kdobros
body: After some other optimizations there may be some redundant waits or not needed event dependencies. This task is to add pass that recalculates event dependencies based on memory dependencies whenever possible. Example input: %ev1 = comp.schedule_read %host from %mem1 on %env comp.wait %ev1 %ev2 = comp.schedule_write %host to %mem2 on %env comp.wait %ev1, %ev2 Expected output: %ev1 = comp.schedule_read %host from %mem1 on %env %ev2 = comp.schedule_write %host to %mem2 on %env wait for %ev1 comp.wait %ev2

title: PlaidMl properly configured, but not running on GPU
author: dkgaraujo
body: Hello PlaidML team! First of all, let me thank all of you for your hard work on PlaidML. I'd like to share an issue I have been facing and for which I did not yet find a solution. When I run the code that you see below, PlaidML tells me INFO:plaidml:Opening device "metal_amd_radeon_pro_5500m.0", but when the model is trained, the GPU is not used. Curiously, when I ran any code with PlaidML + Keras in R, which is essentially a wrapper to the same python environment I tried using in python, the GPU is used. Any light or any guidance you could give me here to be able to use PlaidML with python as well? Many thanks in advance! import os os.environ['KERAS_BACKEND'] = 'plaidml.keras.backend' import keras from keras import layers  max_features = 20000 maxlen = 200  inputs = keras.Input(shape = (maxlen, ), dtype = "int32")  x = layers.Embedding(max_features, 128)(inputs)  #x = layers.Bidirectional(layers.LSTM(64, return_sequences=True))(x) #x = layers.Bidirectional(layers.LSTM(64))(x)  x = layers.LSTM(64, return_sequences = True)(x) x = layers.LSTM(64)(x)  outputs = layers.Dense(1, activation = "sigmoid")(x) model = keras.Model(inputs, outputs) model.summary()  (x_train, y_train), (x_val, y_val) = keras.datasets.imdb.load_data(num_words = max_features)  print(len(x_train), 'Training sequences') print(len(x_val), 'Validation sequences')  x_train = keras.preprocessing.sequence.pad_sequences(x_train, maxlen = maxlen) x_val = keras.preprocessing.sequence.pad_sequences(x_val, maxlen = maxlen)  model.compile('adam',               'binary_crossentropy',               metrics = ['accuracy']) model.fit(x_train, y_train, batch_size = 32, epochs = 2, validation_data = (x_val, y_val))

title: Consider splitting updating vs writing Scatter
author: tzerrell
body: The current Scatter (as of #1610) has a unified API with a parameter controlling whether to override or sum into existing results. For scatters where we know summing isn't needed, we currently need to pass a data tensor for API consistency with summing scatter (rather than for algorithmic reasons). We could instead split scatter into two versions and thereby avoid passing the data tensor to a non-updating scatter. Consider whether we want to make this change. More details available in the linked PR.

title: HOWTO: Steps to install plaidml to Ubuntu 20.04.1 LTS 5.4.0-62-generic with AMD support
author: hapasa
body: I struggled a bit to get plaidml working for up-to-date Ubuntu 20.04.1 LTS machine with Radeon RX550, so I wrote it up to make it easier for others: Steps to install plaidml to Ubuntu 20.04.1 LTS 5.4.0-62-generic with AMD support Locating the latest linux driver for AMD was surpricingly difficult, I got mine from: https://www.amd.com/en/support/kb/release-notes/rn-amdgpu-unified-linux-20-45 That version fixes an issue with 5.4.0-62 kernel, driver released Dec 2020. ./amdgpu-pro-install --opencl=legacy,rocr -y Then create a missing symlink for libOpenCL.so sudo ln -s /opt/amdgpu-pro/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOpenCL.so.1 /opt/amdgpu-pro/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libOpenCL.so sudo ldconfig Then plaidml install: python3 -m venv plaidml-venv source plaidml-venv/bin/activate pip install -U plaidml-keras plaidbench Downgrade h5py to a compatible version: pip install 'h5py<3.0.0' And now plaidml-setup works for me, finding my RX 550 as opencl_amd_gfx804.0 plaidml-setup Benchmark $ plaidbench keras mobilenet Running 1024 examples with mobilenet, batch size 1, on backend plaid INFO:plaidml:Opening device "opencl_amd_gfx804.0" Downloading data from https://github.com/fchollet/deep-learning-models/releases/download/v0.6/mobilenet_1_0_224_tf.h5 17227776/17225924 [==============================] - 1s 0us/step Compiling network... title: custom operator implementation for plaidml
author: artyom-beilis
body: Hello, I'm looking into adding custom kernels/functions to plaidml. Today plaidml has nice feature set but its performance is poor in comparison to cuDNN or MIOpen implementations. I recently started working on dlprimitives project: https://github.com/artyom-beilis/dlprimitives that provides basic functions and inference/training library. Part of it are core components similar to cuDNN but implemented on OpenCL. I implemented GEMM and Winograd based convolutions, GEMM, Batch Normalization and many other operators (some of them https://github.com/artyom-beilis/dlprimitives/blob/master/include/dlprim/core_ops.hpp) My library already vastly outperforms Keras/Plaidml and Caffe/OpenCL and in many cases gives similar performnace to cudnn/hip based caffe or TF. But dlprimitives library isn't as feature reach. I wonder if there any way to integrate these core custom tuned operators into plaidml so its performance can be boosted to reasonable levels? Were need I look into? Thanks!

title: Feature request to support wsl2-GPU-compute /dev/dxg backend
author: hgkamath
body: Firstly, I was just reading on deep-learning, machine learning frameworks, PlaidML etc. So my understanding is still superficial, and I apologize if this bug filing is fully-whack.  With Windows-10 21H2, in Oct 2021, Microsoft is about to release WSL2 (virtual-machine based windows subsystem for linux) with GPU compute feature that provides DirectX direct-compute/direct-ML/cuda support to the Linux WSL2 guest-vm using DXGKRNL driver and /dev/dxg device . This will provide a GPU compute device inside the Linux WSL2 guest-vm. https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/tutorials/gpu-compute https://devblogs.microsoft.com/directx/directx-heart-linux/ The wsl2-GPU-compute requires as WDDM-2.4 compliant graphics-driver, which nvidia kepler series 425 drivers do support. Intel drivers for Haswell GPU-s themselves are only WDDM-2, but in high end laptops they are almost always bundled with a second GPU from nvidia or radeon. In Win10-21H2, the dxg is just a compute backend. In a later win10-WSL2 release, Microsoft may provide paravirtualized graphics GPU support, enabling desktop/GUI. Graphics will require a WDDM-2.9 compliant graphics driver.  ergo, feature request to support WSL2-GPU-compute. If PlaidML uses keras backend, and keras is configured to use tensorflow backend, and if tensorflow is setup to use directml as a backend, and if all works well, then perhaps PlaidML already works inside WSL2 and the issue is moot. One wonders why such long translation chain is required and if at all it will work reliably. Perhaps PlaidML should eliminate keras. A clear documentation somewhere as to how a PlaidML user can get going on WSL2-dxg setup is sufficient. In a related note, eventually, qemu will also have some sort of paravirtualized gpu via the google-venus, mesa, virgl and virtio-gpu subprojects. Please do pen your thoughts regarding future possibilities.

title: Build error possibly caused by setuptools 58.2.0
author: randyppa
body: I am currently attempting to build from source. As background, the reason I am doing this is that I am experiencing issue #168 with the loss:NaN error on all test cases, and in the discussion for that issue one commenter said that building from source fixed the problem. I have successfully gotten to the point of downloading the repository, running ./configure, and then starting bazelisk build //plaidml:wheel. It fails. If I understand the output, the issue is with pystache setup getting a flag 'use_2to3' that it does not support. title: Unable to run pmlc-opt output MLIR example via pmlc-jit
author: alannair
body: I have been attempting to run one of the MLIR examples present in the plaidml-v1 branch of the repo: pmlc/target/x86/tests/reorder_layouts.mlir I wanted to run the main function present in the file, but it takes tensor arguments, so I added a custom function named prospar (with no args or return value) in which tensors are initialized and then passed to main func @prospar() {   %cst = constant 0.000000e+00 : f32   %T0 = linalg.init_tensor [1, 56, 56, 64] : tensor<1x56x56x64xf32>   %1 = linalg.fill(%cst, %T0) : f32, tensor<1x56x56x64xf32> -> tensor<1x56x56x64xf32>   %T1 = linalg.init_tensor [1, 1, 64, 64] : tensor<1x1x64x64xf32>   %2 = linalg.fill(%cst, %T1) : f32, tensor<1x1x64x64xf32> -> tensor<1x1x64x64xf32>   %T2 = linalg.init_tensor [64] : tensor<64xf32>   %3 = linalg.fill(%cst, %T2) : f32, tensor<64xf32> -> tensor<64xf32>   %4 = call @main(%1, %2, %3) : (tensor<1x56x56x64xf32>, tensor<1x1x64x64xf32>, tensor<64xf32>) -> tensor<1x56x56x64xf32>   return }  I first generated the optimized MLIR code via pmlc-opt $ pmlc-opt -split-input-file -x86-reorder-layouts -cse pmlc/target/x86/tests/reorder_layouts.mlir > optimized_code.mlir The contents of optimized_code.mlir of this has been given below (see [1]). I then tried to run the code via  $ pmlc-jit -e prospar -- optimized_code.mlir but that gives me the following error loc("<stdin>":70:1): error: redefinition of attribute alias id 'map0' PLEASE submit a bug report to https://bugs.llvm.org/ and include the crash backtrace. Stack dump: 0.	Program arguments: pmlc-jit -e prospar Stack dump without symbol names (ensure you have llvm-symbolizer in your PATH or set the environment var `LLVM_SYMBOLIZER_PATH` to point to it): pmlc-jit(+0x959c64)[0x55b67d6d1c64] pmlc-jit(+0x95764e)[0x55b67d6cf64e] /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0(+0x153c0)[0x7facc53df3c0] pmlc-jit(+0x7064e8)[0x55b67d47e4e8] pmlc-jit(+0xbaf64f)[0x55b67d92764f] pmlc-jit(+0x66fac9)[0x55b67d3e7ac9] pmlc-jit(+0x6723fc)[0x55b67d3ea3fc] pmlc-jit(+0x6801e7)[0x55b67d3f81e7] pmlc-jit(+0x6697e4)[0x55b67d3e17e4] pmlc-jit(+0x39756c)[0x55b67d10f56c] pmlc-jit(+0x31983d)[0x55b67d09183d] /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(__libc_start_main+0xf3)[0x7facc4e5f0b3] pmlc-jit(+0x39679e)[0x55b67d10e79e] Segmentation fault (core dumped)  The first line of this error attributes the cause to redefinition of map0 (which indeed has been redefined both in reorder_layouts.mlir and in optimized_code.mlir. I tried working around this by removing everything from reorder_layouts.mlir below the main function, effectively removing the map redefinition (see [2]). Now when I do the same as above: $ pmlc-opt -split-input-file -x86-reorder-layouts -cse pmlc/target/x86/tests/reorder_layouts.mlir | pmlc-jit -e prospar I get a different error: loc("<stdin>":10:3): error: cannot be converted to LLVM IR: missing `LLVMTranslationDialectInterface` registration for dialect for op: builtin.func ERROR: could not convert to LLVM IR  What are these errors, why are they popping up and how do I resolve this? title: Implement Data Parallelism
author: brianretford
body: PlaidML currently aborts when multiple devices are selected. Initial support for multiple devices will be implemented through a data parallel approach, using something similar to MXNet's strategy. Possible Implementation Strategy:  Add a setting for parallelism strategy, with two options [None, Data]. None matches current behavior Modify the program.cc in local_platform to take a list of devices and the parallelism strategy. If data parallelism is enabled, do the work necessary to build multiple kernels and split work amongst them Need to figure out how to shoehorn this into keras - splitting batches into parts and rejoining seems like the most reasonable approach

title: Support Multiple Devices
author: brianretford
body: PlaidML currently requires exactly one selected device. We've considered multiple approaches to multi-device support:  [Data Parallelism] (Multiple copies of the function graph on each device, coordinate weight updates) Model Parallelism (Split up the graph across devices) Kernel Parallelism (Effectively splitting up the Tile Op index space)  Alternatively, we could implement backends for frameworks that have solid multi-device support, such as:  MXNet TensorFlow  This is a parent issue tracking implementation of all 3. We'll start with data parallelism and move on to others as warranted, with separate issues for each.

title: MaxPooling2D in Keras fails due to TypeError in backend
author: phrz
body: I do not claim to even slightly understand the inner workings of Keras or PlaidML, but I was determined to hunt this issue down. Whenever I tried to add a keras MaxPooling2D layer to a Sequential, I received the following error: TypeError: can only concatenate tuple (not "list") to tuple  Attributed to this line in plaidml/keras/backend.py: outshape = x.shape[:2] + num_out_size Without understanding much of the surrounding code, other than that its purpose was to generate Tile code, I found that x.shape resulted in a tuple (None, 1), yet num_out_size was an array of integers. After some educated guessing, I changed the line to this: outshape = list(x.shape[:2]) + num_out_size and no longer received the error. I am running plaidml 0.1.2, keras 2.0.8, plaidml-keras 0.1.2, on Python 3.6.3 installed through Homebrew (brew install python3) on a Mac running macOS 10.13. I produced the following example code to reproduce the error. import plaidml.keras plaidml.keras.install_backend()  import keras from keras.models import Sequential from keras.layers import Reshape, MaxPooling2D, Conv2D  model = Sequential()  model.add( 	Reshape( 		(1, 64, 64),      		input_shape=(1, 64*64) 	) )  model.add( 	Conv2D( 		filters=3, 		kernel_size=(5,5), 		padding='same', 		activation='relu' 	) )  model.add( 	MaxPooling2D(pool_size=(2,2), data_format='channels_first') ) I cannot guarantee that this is a minimal example, it is just a very faithful recreation of the original code that triggered the error, with hardcoded values instead of external variables. If I am misguided in submitting this issue, which I do not doubt, please point me in the right direction. I just wanted to see if this problem could be fixed through a little tinkering.

title: RNNs require static sequence length
author: tzerrell
body: Recurrent networks currently require the sequence length to be known when the Tile code is constructed and bound. This requires the shape of the input layer for RNNs to have a specific size for their time dimension (i.e., not a None in the time dimension of their shape). This excludes a few use cases, and also breaks Keras networks that infer the sequence length automatically. The latter case has a workaround -- explicitly specify the sequence length in the input fed into the RNN (e.g. explicitly specifying the shape in an Input layer); but it would be better to not require a workaround.

title: Question about supporting CPUs and accelerators
author: romix
body: PlaidML looks very interesting. It is very impressive that it can quickly produce very efficient kernels without providing any manual scheduling descriptions like e.g. in case of TVM or Halide! But I've got a couple of questions about supporting CPUs and accelerators:   The internal representation and the model of a target in PlaidML seems to be rather OpenCL-like. It is not quite clear how well CPUs are supported by this approach. E.g. is the provided code generation for CPUs as good as for GPUs? Are there any benchmarks on CPUs comparing it with e.g. TF, Caffe2, TVM, Halide, etc?   Is it possible for PlaidML to support more complex kinds of targets like e.g. custom accelerators, which often have more layers of the memory hierarchy than OpenCL devices, a number of dedicated multipliers for tensors of specific sizes, support for quantized tensors, etc?  How would one model memory buffers at different levels of the memory hierarchy? How would one model e.g. explicit transfers between the host memory and target memory or between different levels of the target's memory hierarchy? Are there any plans for improvements in this area? Is PlaidML/Tile expressive enough to support such targets? Which parts of PlaidML codebase would need to be extended to support those targets? Would it need any conceptual changes (e.g. introducing new kinds of abstractions for memory hierarchy layers, etc) or just adding a new backend? How much would the increased target complexity affect e.g. the current PlaidML code for generating efficient kernels?

title: Pseudo-random generation from tiles
author: vermorel
body: Random number generation is used for weight initialization in deep learning. It is also used for all sort of learning techniques (eg. dropout) during the execution itself. Yet, it does not seem that the tile language offers any support for pseudo-random number generation. This feature would be useful. Also, such a feature was to happen, I would suggest (difficult) to make it possible to ensure that the execution remains deterministic. Indeed, real randomness complicates debugging, as bugs become Heisenbugs. Thus, it would be nice to have control on the seeding mechanism of the pseudo-random generator.

title: OpenCL on Mac produces incorrect training results
author: monogenea
body: Hi guys. After following the instructions for installing plaidml on my iMac Pro, I originally chose opencl_amd_amd_radeon_vega_56, confirmed the selection in the ~/.plaidml file, and successfully deployed plaidml as the backend for Keras using both R and Python. Runtime of CNN benchmarks was substantially shorter, as expected. The problem, however, was that the actual optimisation was going mental, with training loss increasing, rather than decreasing, indefinitely and concluding with reported missing accuracy - overall a strange behaviour, as you see. After looking into many different potential causes, I found that replacing the opencl_amd_amd_radeon_vega_56 option by the metal_amd_radeon_vega_56 one maintained the performance gain on GPU usage and also rendered accurate loss minimisation, with overall accuracy comparable to benchmarks (i.e. Keras MNIST, CIFAR10 and the like). Maybe there was something obvious about the options that I missed; it would be great to hear from other users with the same specs.

title: Cannot use custom activation function (SineReLU) from Keras-Contrib
author: wilderrodrigues
body: Hi, I have been using Keras + TensorFlow for more than 2 years now. It is a good combination, except when one needs to try out quick experiments on a MacBook and it doesn't use the AMD Radeon GPUs. Hence, kudos for your work on PlaidML, which I discover a couple of weeks ago. I'm currently using PlaidML + Keras to train custom models, using CNNs, LSTMs and GRUs architectures. All works fine. However, when trying to use the SineReLU, a custom activation function that is part of Keras Contrib, it unfortunately breaks. Based on the error message, it seems that the DerivDefines is not able to compute the sin function, which is used by the SineReLU. I traced the error back to this code snippet in the symbolic.cc file:   auto it = DerivDefines.find(op->fn());   if (it == DerivDefines.end()) {     throw std::runtime_error("Invalid derivative: unknown function " + op->fn());   }  And the unknown function is the sin function, as I mentioned above. How hard would be to get it implemented? Keras Contrib contains many other implementations that would depend on sin/cos functions. Looking forward to hear from you and if help is needed, please let me know. Cheers, Wilder

title: Multiple easy backend function implementations
author: SleepProgger
body: I implemented some of the missing keras.backend functions (the easy ones) and love to have some feedback. No PR yet, because i am not sure about some of them (and didn't feel like writing test cases tbh ;)) Some open questions:  Is there anything i missed for the any and all implementations ? They feel a bit hackish, but should work well. Do i see that right that all the random function without _variable at the end should be executed on the device and thus create new outputs for every call ? Whereas the ones with _variable at the end of the name should only be created once ? When should the result be a constant and when a variable ? Is there even a difference with plaidml backends ? The arange impl fe: returns a constant. Is this the correct approach ? Is my handling of dtypes for functions which create wrapped numpy values correct ? The idea is that both tile.Dtype and np.dtype + strings are accepted. Is there a reason that variable doesn't use the dtype of the np.array (if that is the input) even when the variable dtype parameter is set to None ? Probably more question i missed, but see TODOs  def any(x, axis=None, keepdims=False):     # Should probably check if int* or bool ?     truths = plaidml.op.summation(x, axis, keepdims, floatx=plaidml.DType.INT32)     return not truths > 0   def all(x, axis=None, keepdims=False):     # Should probably check if int* or bool ?     truths = plaidml.op.summation(x, axis, keepdims, floatx=plaidml.DType.INT32)     if axis is None:         # == and != (magic functions) doesn't seem to be implemented for plaidml tensor/variables         # why not ? The magic functions for lt and gt seem to be implemented. + equal and not_equal works          items = np.prod(x.shape.dims)         return K.equal(truths, items)     return K.equal(truths, x.shape.dims[axis])   def arange(start, stop=None, step=1, dtype='int32'):     # basically iperovs impl     try:         dtype = ptile.convert_pml_dtype_to_np(dtype)     except ValueError: pass     return K.constant( np.arange(start, stop, step, dtype), dtype=dtype)   class CumulativeProd(ptile.Operation):     """Cumulative product of a tensor"""      def __init__(self, x, axis=0):         ranges = ', '.join(['N{}'.format(n) for n in range(x.shape.ndims)])         dest_idxs = ', '.join(['i{}'.format(n) for n in range(x.shape.ndims)])         src_idxs = ['i{}'.format(n) for n in range(x.shape.ndims)]         src_idxs[axis] += ' - k'         src_idxs = ', '.join(src_idxs)         f = """             function (I[{src_ranges}]) -> (O) {{                 O[{dest_idxs}: {dest_ranges}] = *(I[{src_idxs}]), k < N{ax};             }}""".format(             src_ranges=ranges, dest_idxs=dest_idxs, dest_ranges=ranges, src_idxs=src_idxs, ax=axis)         super(CumulativeProd, self).__init__(f, [('I', x)], [('O', x.shape)])  cumprod = CumulativeProd.function   def eye(size, dtype=None, name=None):     # TODO: I am not sure if that is a good idea to use np here instead of generating this on the device .?     if dtype is None:         dtype = K.floatx()     else:         try:             dtype = ptile.convert_pml_dtype_to_np(dtype)         except ValueError: pass     return K.constant(np.eye(size, dtype=dtype), name=name, dtype=dtype)   def random_normal_variable(shape, mean, scale, dtype=None, name=None, seed=None):     if seed is not None:         np.random.seed(seed)     if dtype is None:         dtype = K.floatx()     else:         try:             dtype = ptile.convert_pml_dtype_to_np(dtype)         except ValueError: pass     data = np.random.normal(mean, scale, shape).astype(dtype)     return K.variable(data)   def sign(data):     return ptile.unary_op(data, "I == 0 ? 0 : (I > 0 ? 1 : -1)", name="Sign")  def stack(x, axis=0):     tshape = x[0].shape     for item in x:         if tshape != item.shape:             raise ValueError("All inputs must have the same shape and type")     nshape = list(tshape.dims)     nshape.insert(axis if axis >= 0 else len(nshape), 1)     return K.concatenate([K.reshape(item, nshape) for item in x], axis=axis)  Possible fixes for: #271

title: dropout backend function wrong ?
author: SleepProgger
body: The tile code for the backend function dropout looks like: function (I, X, L) -> (O) {         R = 1.0 - L;         M = 1.0 / R;         O = (prng_value(I) < R ? X * M : 0.0);     }  and as keras Dropout layer simply returns the result of the dropout function this leads to not only to values dropped (like expected) but also to a multiplication with (1 / (1-Level)) for not dropped values. If my understanding is correct that is the wrong behavior. Simple fix is replace X * M with a simple X Demo:     in_ = v = keras.layers.Input((5, 5, 1), dtype="float32")     v = keras.layers.Dropout(0.5)(v)     func = K.function([in_, K.learning_phase()],[v])     print(func((np.ones((1, 5, 5, 1), dtype="float32"), 1)))  Result [array([[[[2.],          [0.],          [0.],          [0.],          [2.]],          [[2.],          [0.],          [0.],          [0.],          [0.]],          [[2.],          [0.],          [0.],          [0.],          [2.]],          [[2.],          [2.],          [2.],          [0.],          [2.]],          [[0.],          [0.],          [2.],          [0.],          [0.]]]], dtype=float32)]

title: Ngraph with plaidml backend leads to invalid opencl kernel
author: SleepProgger
body: When using a self compiled version of ngraph-tf to test ngraph with the plaidml backend i ran into some invalid generated opencl kernels because floor is called with integer parameter which leads to 'floor' is ambiguous errors. I used a slightly changed version of the keras example from ngraph-tf: import tensorflow as tf from keras.applications.resnet50 import ResNet50, preprocess_input, decode_predictions import numpy as np import sys  if __name__ == '__main__':     if len(sys.argv) < 2:         print("USAGE: %s NGRAPH_backend or NONE" % sys.argv[0])         exit()     if sys.argv[1] != "NONE":         import ngraph_bridge         print("Supported ngraph backend:\n  %s" % "\n  ".join(ngraph_bridge.list_backends()))         ngraph_bridge.set_backend(sys.argv[1])         print("Using ngraph backend %s" % ngraph_bridge.get_currently_set_backend_name())      # A simple script to run inference and training on resnet 50     model = ResNet50(weights='imagenet')          batch_size = 8     img = np.random.rand(batch_size, 224, 224, 3)     preds = model.predict(preprocess_input(img))     print('Predicted:', decode_predictions(preds, top=3)[0])     model.compile("SGD", loss='categorical_crossentropy')     preds = model.fit(         preprocess_input(img), np.zeros((batch_size, 1000), dtype='float32'))     print('Ran a train round')  When being executed like python KERAS_BACKEND="tensorflow" python test_ngraph_bridge.py PLAIDML this leads to this output: https://gist.github.com/SleepProgger/c8c2ece66d6aed3010ff83c7c029b166 The error happens at the training phase, prediction works fine. This is the same behaviour as this snippet produces with keras->plaidml: K.floor(K.constant(np.zeros(10, dtype=int), dtype=plaidml.DType.INT32)).eval() As there is no point ever to call floor on integer maybe the HAL or Tile should noop all floor calls with integer inputs (Same problem with ceil btw). I am having some other problems with the ngraph-tf bridge, but that might be my fault because i used py3.7 instead of py3.5. This example ran ok via keras->tf->ngraph->cpu, keras->tf and keras->plaidml tho.

title: Add verbose logging through an environment variable
author: denise-k
body: We've had several cases of issues that required verbose logging to debug. Currently, PlaidML has support for verbose logging, but it must be set using a function that is called after the PlaidML binaries are loaded. This makes it difficult to debug exceptions that occur in the following cases:  Developers who want to set verbose logging without having to modify their source code or PlaidML binaries Developers who are debugging plaidml-setup issues that occur during the binary loading process Developers who are debugging issues between nGraph <-> PlaidML  In all of these cases, verbose logging could be easily enabled through an environment variable that the user sets in their shell before setting up PlaidML. We should add support and documentation for this.

author: lllyasviel

title: Cache transform in PXA
author: jbruestle
body: Write a transformation functions which 'cache' loads/reduces so that the operate out of 'local' memory for a certain tile size.  More specifically, implement functions: LogicalResult CacheLoad(AffineParallelOp par, AffineLoadOp load) LogicalResult CacheReduce(AffineParallelOp par, AffineReduceOp red)  which construct a properly sized local allocation inside the body of  and then for the load case, load the values from the original memref into the local buffer, and replace the original load with a load from the local buffer.  For reduce, the case is similar, but the initial allocation must also be initialized the the reduction identity and the a final reduce performed at the end.

title: Limited PXA vectorization transform + pass
author: jbruestle
body: Write a limited vectorization transform for PXA with the following interface: LogicalResult performVectorization(AffineParallelOp op, BlockArgument index, unsigned vecSize);  Example: // Original  affine.parallel (%i, %j, %k) = (0, 0, 0) to (64, 64, 66) {     %a = affine.load %X[%i, %k] : memref<64x64xf32>     %b = affine.load %Y[%k, %j] : memref<64x64xf32>     %c = mul %a, %b : f32     pxa.reduce add %c, %Z[%i, %j] : memref<64x64xf32> }  // Vectorized over j, size = 8 affine.parallel (%i, %j, %k) = (0, 0, 0) to (64, 64, 66) step (1, 8, 1) {     %a = affine.load %X[%i, %k] : memref<64x64xf32>     %a2 = vector.broadcast %a : vector<8xf32>     %b = affine.vector_load %Y[%k, %j] : memref<64x64xf32>, vector<8xf32>     %c = mul %a, %b : vector<8xf32>     pxa.vector_reduce add %c, %Z[%i, %j] : memref<64x64xf32> }  It's OK to simply fail in the following cases for the initial version:  The affine.parallel has anything besides loads/reduces or scalar ops (i.e. fmul, etc). The range of the index to vectorize on is not divisible by the vector size Any of the loads is not stride 1 or stride 0 with respect to the index to vectorize over Any reduce is not stride 1 with respect to the vector index. The step for the index being vectorized is not 1  Additionally, provide a trivial vectorization pass for testing that simply trys to vectorize over each index in order for each top level parallel for.

title: Move affine.load + affine.vector_load into pxa
author: jbruestle
body: Currently there are a number of issues with and affine.load and pxa.reduce (which are basically the 'read' and 'write' of pxa) being in distinct code bases.  Specifically: we currently cannot fix typing issues related to memref-state, we cannot add memory analysis / memref-state tracing interfaces, and generally the two operations are at slightly different levels of abstraction.  By moving the affine.load -> pxa.load we will be able to address these issues.

title: Subgroup transformation
author: jbruestle
body: Add a PXA transformation the rewrites an affine.parallel in a similar fashion to the v0 subgroup pass.  The transformation takes a 'plan' produced by an analysis method (still to be ported), and performs the following transformations:  Tile the affine.parallel (where the inner tile memory usage for both read + write will be registers) Vectorize on the primary subgroup index Perform a vector load transform on secondary subgroup indexes Tile via TileAccumulations Cache loads inside the accumulate loop Cache reduces outside the accumulate loop

title: Create 'TileAccumulation' pass and add to the GPU pipeline.
author: jbruestle
body: Currently lowering to GPU has bugs due the racing writes cause by invalid kernel outlining of serial affine.for into parallel code.  While this bug need to be addressed, it highlights the need for ordering affine.parallel loops into two sets of indexs, one that is parallel safe post lowering of pxa.reduce, and one that is not.  To perform this function, we will add a new transform function as well as a pass. Steps:   Move the utility function TileAccumulation (prototyped here:                plaidml/pmlc/dialect/pxa/transforms/subgroups.cc                    Line 127       in       be4c0cb                                                 void TileAccumulations(AffineParallelOp op) {                    ), into a free function in a new header/c++ pair pmlc/dialect/pxa/transforms/tile_accumulation*   Add a pass (and add to the gpu pipeline) which performs TileAccumulation followed by a CacheWrite (see #1239)   This will make the outermost affine.parallel thread safe.

body: We need a way to store constant buffers on a per-module basis. Constant buffers need to have a lifetime that matches their usage within a module. So there are two invalidation events:  When there are no longer any ops referring to a constant buffer. When a module is destroyed, all constant buffers in that module should be destroyed.  A new ConstantBufferMgr singleton is proposed with the following API:  int64_t createBuffer(ModuleOp module, BufferPtr buffer): returns a unique ID void destroyBuffer(ModuleOp module, int64_t bufferId): destroy the specified buffer void destroyModule(ModuleOp module): destroy all buffers on the specified module BufferPtr resolveBuffer(ModuleOp module, int64_t bufferId): resolve the specified buffer  Also create a new OwningModuleRef which calls mgr->destroyModule(*this) in the destructor of the module. Add a cleanup pass which makes a sweep of all constant ops and calls mgr->destroyBuffer(module, bufferId) on each unreferenced buffer. Modify existing EDSL constants so that they come in as ConstantOp rather than a program argument.

title: Subgroup cost model analysis/fixes (part 2)
author: adstraw
body: This is a continuation of issue #1379.   Summary of that issue:  The subgroup cost model was improved by porting some ideas from PlaidML V0 to V1:  1. calculation of register usage 2. modeling of cache misses and 3. calculation of memory IO.  The new V1 subgroup cost model assumes a memory bounded computation and uses cost = memory IO / total computation.  Results:  ResNet50 inference time on Intel Gen9 was improved 10-20%. The previous issue (1379) also uncovered a technique called "semi scan" (as opposed to full scan) of tiles.  A full scan looks at all possible tile combinations and takes quite a lot of time --- days.  A semi scan looks only at tile combinations where register usage does not exceed some maximum and runs fairly quickly --- minutes.  For many layers in ResNet50 it was found that 128 registers served as effective upper bound.  Effective = able to complete a semi scan in a reasonable amount of time and find all / most of the fastest kernels. Attached is a semi scan of ResNet50 layer 2a, branch 2a. layer_2a_branch_2a_semi_scan.xlsx Some basics on the convolution: Input = NHWCi = 1x56x56x64 Kernel =  HWCiCo = 1x1x64x64 Output = NHWCo = 1x56x56x64 And, some details about the columns in the scan: A,B,C - Register, accesses, cache misses as calculated by computeMemoryInfo D - Selected plan = subgroup size:[inner tile]:[subgroup tile] G,H,J - MB cost = Mem IO / TotOps K - Kernel times L,M,N,O - ASM file generated + spill and bank conflict info NOTE:  Columns E,F,I have to do with compute bound "goodness" (as opposed to memory bound cost).  Ignoring these for the moment.  Proceeding with the (wrong) assumption that all computation is memory bound for simplicity.  That should roughly be true for ResNet50 layer 2a, branch 2a. Problem statement:  The current cost model is doing a poor job of locating the fastest kernels.  Here are the top 10 fastest kernels alongside the memory bound (MB) cost which have a wide variance:    MB Cost Kernel Time     13.6368 0.096   3.76694 0.103333   3.41927 0.105   18.3087 0.1105   13.6368 0.110583   18.3087 0.110666   24.065 0.11325   17.0531 0.11425   17.2324 0.11775   17.0531 0.12625    All of the above kernels are considered "memory bounded" so the assumption that all kernels are memory bounded holds, so far.  The lowest memory bound cost among all kernels was 1.188.

title: Feedback on build documentation
author: rengolin
body: Trying to build from the docs got me some figuring out, so I propose we update the docs to include the other stuff. But before I submit a docs change, I'd like to know what of those "figuring out" things are "commonly known", assumed or just me not getting it right. So, here's a list of things I had to do in addition to the base docs:  After installing conda, I have created a script that enters/leaves the virtualenv, as I don't want to enter it on login (its default behaviour is to add it to .bashrc, which is silly). Basically, I moved what conda added to .bashrc into a new script, and added two new aliases: alias enter-plaidml='source plaidml-env-script' and alias leave-plaidml='conda deactivate'. To allow OpenMP testing, PlaidML needs llvm-lit, FileCheck and not on the PATH, but the llvm-project-build directory didn't have it. I have built LLVM+Clang+MLIR on my box and copied the files to a directory in the PATH (same as the env script). I don't know how that directory is pulled from, but it would be nice to have them there and maybe even automatically add it to the PATH. I created an Ubuntu 22.04 container, and when running ./configure I was told there's no support for OpenCV on that distro (even though I can install its packages, so I'm confused). The interim solution is to run ./configure --no_openvino. The docs don't mention submodules, but the two directories under vendor (mlir-hlo and openvino) don't get initialised by default. I suggest adding a step to git submodule update --init --recursive before calling ./configure. I had no ccache on my container, but the build system still chose to use it, then I got a ccache: not found when building. I just installed ccache (and clang and lld for good measure), but it would be good to only use it when it's on the PATH. Installing clang and adding export CC=clang CXX=clang++ didn't make configure choose it for the build.  After the CMake is done, I get a nice message on how to run the unit tests, but the build has many error messages like: ../../plaidml/core/core.h:93:5: error: 'fn' cannot be used as a function ../../plaidml/core/core.h: In instantiation of 'void plaidml::ffi::call_void(F, Args ...) [with F = int; Args = {void (*)(plaidml_error*, plaidml_expr*, long unsigned int, plaidml_dim_expr**), plaidml_expr*, long unsigned int, plaidml_dim_expr**}]':  ../../plaidml/op/lib/ops.cc: In function 'plaidml::edsl::Value plaidml::op::lib::variance(const plaidml::edsl::Value&)': ../../plaidml/op/lib/ops.cc:3629:33: error: no matching function for call to 'plaidml::edsl::Value::Value(<brace-enclosed initializer list>)'  3629 |   return Value{SumSqDiff / denom};       |                                 ^  ../../plaidml/op/lib/ops.cc:3338:17: error: no matching function for call to 'plaidml::edsl::TensorDim::TensorDim()'  3338 |       TensorDim G, C, K;       |                 ^  /usr/include/c++/11/type_traits:955:52: error: static assertion failed: template argument must be a complete class or an unbounded array   955 |       static_assert(std::__is_complete_or_unbounded(__type_identity<_Tp>{}),       |                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~  IIUC, all errors have plenty of candidates, which means the compiler's ability to guess the types is going wrong. This is using ccache c++ which defaults to gcc, and the version on my system is 11.2.0. I found no way to change it to clang. I think the docs should mention how to create the environment that is known to work (ex. Ubuntu 20.04), so that people with newer OSs don't try to chase weird build errors. Creating a docker that has that environment would be a nice touch, too.

title: Evaluate Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO)
author: zamazan4ik
body: Hi! Recently I checked Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) improvements on multiple projects. The results are here. LLVM-related results are here could be also interesting to you since LLVM is a dependency for PlaidML. Since PGO showed measurable improvements in compiler-like loads (CPython, Clang, Clangd, clang-format, GCC, Rustc, etc.) I think it could be useful to check PGO on PlaidML as well. We need to perform PGO benchmarks on PlaidML. And if it shows improvements - add a note about possible improvements in PlaidML performance with PGO. Providing an easier way (e.g. a build option) to build scripts with PGO can be useful for the end-users too. Maybe testing Post-Link Optimization techniques (like LLVM BOLT from Facebook) would be interesting too but I recommend starting from the usual PGO. Not sure where would be better to start in the case of PlaidML. Probably (but I could be wrong) compiler and JIT implementation are the good starting candidates.
